clue.text: Is outwardly better when played by ear

indicators.note: the synonym for better sits on the outside, wrapping round the word Is

parts.note: to better something is to improve it, past form improved
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone whose musical playing gets better when done without sheet music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' looks like it describes Is, but it says the synonym for better wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Music played by ear is made up on the spot rather than read from a score.

clue.text: Out of form — but not as a golfer

definitions.meaning: feeling below one's usual standard of health or performance
for a golfer, scoring below the standard number of strokes is a good thing, not a sign of poor form

explanation.definitionFit: Feeling below standard is a common idiom, while in golf the phrase means beating the expected stroke count.

clue.text: Unexpected result of Parnell's policy

indicators.note: an unexpected outcome is a turn-up, so the letters of the next word come out in a surprising order

explanation.surface: A historical comment on the unforeseen consequence of an Irish politician's programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Stewart Parnell led the 19th-century campaign for Irish Home Rule; the Protestant north-east province resisted it, ending up separately governed.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern Irish province whose Unionist resistance was a historical consequence of the Home Rule campaign.

clue.text: Cinderella's sisters were so unfair

definitions.meaning: in pantomime the heroine's stepsisters are traditionally hideous
read as un-fair, the opposite of fair-looking or beautiful

explanation.definitionFit: Pantomime's stepsisters are famously unattractive, and not fair in the sense of good-looking means plain.

clue.text: Festive gatherings of runners?

parts.note: sounds like parties for athletes, but the runners are runner beans, so this is a banquet of the vegetable

explanation.definitionFit: A British slang term for a jolly celebration or outing, literally a meal of beans.

clue.text: Become a success and travel

definitions.meaning: an idiom for doing well in one's career
literally to visit lots of locations

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to prosper, and taken literally means visiting many destinations.

clue.text: A piece played in a mask?

definitions.meaning: a rectangular tile laid in a game of spots
a small half-mask worn at a masquerade, with a hooded cloak

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a spotted game tile and a masquerade half-mask with cloak.

clue.text: Gathering for a drink, we hear

indicators.note: says the next word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: bevvy is British slang for an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A group meeting up at the pub for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A group, especially of birds or girls, gathered together; a collective noun.

clue.text: The address of a single person

definitions.text: The address of a single person

parts.words: The address of a single person
parts.note: looks like an unmarried person's home location, but address means a speech given by one speaker

explanation.definitionFit: A long speech delivered by one person alone is a solo address.

clue.text: Snooze — head drops — rest could be a tonic

indicators.note: what is left of the word may be rearranged into something else
the first letter of the word Snooze is lost

explanation.surface: Taking a nap with your head nodding forward as a restorative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head drops' removes S from Snooze, leaving NOOZE; 'rest could be' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracing seaside air was popularly called this gas and thought to be invigorating, a tonic.

clue.text: Critical stage of increasing gravity for spacemen

definitions.text: Critical stage of increasing gravity for spacemen

parts.words: Critical stage of increasing gravity for spacemen
parts.note: gravity reads as seriousness, but here it is the pull felt when astronauts return into the atmosphere

explanation.definitionFit: The dangerous return of a spacecraft into Earth's atmosphere, where gravitational pull increases.

clue.text: It's fully in order; make nothing of it

indicators.note: putting the letters in order means rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something is all correct, so there's nothing to make a fuss about.
explanation.definitionFit: To render void or cancel is to reduce something to nothing.

clue.text: It creeps through by six

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral for six
per is Latin for by, as in per annum

explanation.surface: Something crawling through at six o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake, which creeps along the ground; a venomous adder.

clue.text: Customised Porsche, original wings, about three years old

indicators.note: a car customised has been altered, so its letters are rearranged
the wings of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A modified sports car with its original bodywork wings, of a certain vintage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wings' takes O and L from original; with PORSCHE they are rearranged by 'Customised'.
explanation.definitionFit: A child too young for school, typically around three or four, is described this way.

clue.text: Accommodating a small number in new premises

indicators.note: the small number goes inside the rearranged letters
a new version of the word is a rearrangement

parts.note: IV, Roman four, is a small number

explanation.surface: Fitting a few people into newly acquired business property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accommodating' looks like the container signal, but it is the definition; 'in' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: An easygoing, accommodating attitude is a tolerant, allowing one.

clue.text: Ancient city captured in erudite books

indicators.note: the city is held inside the synonym for erudite

parts.note: erudite means well-read, literate
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, a crossword staple

explanation.surface: An old city's history recorded in scholarly volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Written works collectively, such as books, form a body of writing.

clue.text: Keeping in shape, being opposed to psychiatry

definitions.meaning: describes fabric that does not contract in the wash
a shrink is slang for a psychiatrist, so one resisting them

explanation.definitionFit: Fabric that keeps its size in the wash, and humorously someone fighting their psychiatrist.

clue.text: They're intended to encourage laying in little savings

definitions.meaning: dummy eggs left in a hen's nest to prompt her to lay
money put aside for the future

explanation.definitionFit: Fake eggs placed to induce hens to lay, and figuratively a sum set aside in reserve.

clue.text: Sailor banished to quarters for being a defaulter

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
sent away, as in sent to Coventry
E (east) is a compass quarter, here taken twice

explanation.surface: A seaman sent off to his quarters as punishment for some offence.
explanation.definitionFit: One who fails to turn up when required, defaulting on attendance.

clue.text: Power lines that may last for many years

definitions.text: Power lines that may last for many years

parts.words: Power lines that may last for many years
parts.note: looks like electricity cables, but power lines are successions of ruling families

explanation.definitionFit: Successive rulers from one family, holding power over generations.

clue.text: He's stupid in trying to open it without a key

indicators.note: the answer is held in the stretch of letters across the words that follow

explanation.surface: A fool fumbling at a locked door with no key.
explanation.walkthrough: The run lies across 'open it without'; the surface pictures a fool fumbling at a locked door.
explanation.definitionFit: A foolish, dim person, the kind of fool a mild insult names.

clue.text: He keeps on accumulating endless unhappiness

indicators.note: the synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: misery means unhappiness

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps piling up sorrow without end.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarder of money who keeps stockpiling and never spends.

clue.text: Girl turns tail at the docks

indicators.note: the last two letters of the name swap places

parts.note: Marian is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman runs away from the waterfront.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour with moorings for yachts and small boats, a set of docks.

clue.text: Overhead branches

parts.note: looks like boughs of trees above, but means branching horns on a deer's head

explanation.definitionFit: The branched horns of a deer grow from the head like boughs.

clue.text: He fell out of sympathy with his partner

definitions.text: He fell out of sympathy with his partner

parts.words: He fell out of sympathy with his partner
parts.note: seems to describe a quarrel, but refers to the biblical Fall, sharing the forbidden fruit with Eve

explanation.definitionFit: The first man in Genesis, who fell from grace alongside Eve.

clue.text: The Crown takes a firm course, if backed

parts.note: CO, company, is a firm

indicators.note: the word for course is read backwards

parts.note: tenor means general course or drift

explanation.surface: The monarchy taking a resolute line, if supported.
explanation.definitionFit: A small crown worn by nobility.

clue.text: New Jersey?

parts.note: seems to be the American state, but is a newborn of the Channel Island cattle breed

explanation.definitionFit: A young cow, such as the newborn of a Jersey cow.

clue.text: Maturing drink in silver container

indicators.note: the drink sits in the silver acting as container

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A spirit left to mature in a silver vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing older and mellowing, as wine or spirits do.

clue.text: Soldier to offer information unasked

definitions.meaning: one who enlists of their own free will
to say something without being asked

explanation.definitionFit: Both an unpaid enlisting soldier and the verb for proffering something unprompted.
